answer: In an agent economy routing cargo, each agent must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid on a voyage through a bridge or inlet. Each bond grants one bidding slot, and the same funds cannot back multiple identities. An attacker can create names freely, but activating 1,000 sybils requires tying up $100,000 for a month, sacrificing liquidity and interest. The defense makes usable identities costly even when creating accounts is free.
